newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean opposition say will ratify OECD admission.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean opposition say will ratify OECD admission.

text.p: South Korea's opposition parties agreed on Tuesday to support membership in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), party officials said.
Seoul was invited to join the Paris-based club of rich nations on October 11, but opposition parties had threatened to block ratification in the parliament.

On Tuesday, parliamentary representatives of South Korea's three main political parties -- the ruling New Korea Party and the opposition National Congress for New Politics and the United Liberal Democrats -- signed an agreement to bring the issue to a vote on November 26, they said.
Spokesmen for the opposition parties confirmed their members would vote in favour.

Opposition parties were not opposed to OECD membership in principle, but said they wanted a delay because the country's troubled economy could not withstand the shock of further market liberalisation.
South Korea would be the second Asian member nation of the club after Japan, and the first from the region's newly industrialising economies.
Since applying for OECD membership in March 1995, South Korea has sped up liberalisation of its financial markets to foreign investors and pledged further reforms.

But opposition parties and critics have argued the rapid opening of the fledgling financial markets could deal a serious blow to the economy, already suffering from a yawning foreign trade deficit and inflationary pressures.
The South Korean government projects the nation's current account deficit to rise to $20 billion in calendar 1996 from a shortfall of $8.9 billion in 1995.
